sourceReviews.supportingSummary: Tags are user-facing mutable references. Their component spelling alone does not make them immutable; the question therefore needs its stated nonreuse policy rather than attributing immutability to ACR.

The training separates producing pipeline run IDs from source commit identity, recommends combining identifiers for traceability, and defines nonreused deployment references. It does not explicitly recommend a build-system prefix; the proposed pair is a conditional inference from those meanings and this stem.

A changed base image can cause an application rebuild without an application source change. This supports why the same commit is insufficient to distinguish the producing executions specified in the scenario.

choiceReviews.rationale: Tagging lines 81 and 89 distinguish execution identity from source-state identity; Tasks lines 93–97 supports a base-driven rebuild. The stem expressly allows two builds of one commit after different patches, so commit identity alone can collide for the required per-execution reference. A commit tag remains valid for source traceability, but source-only identity is not the requested invariant.

The documented build-ID and combined-tag patterns support preserving execution metadata, while nonreuse preserves the resulting reference. Derivation: represent a producing execution by (system identity, local build ID). Different systems are distinguished by the first component; distinct runs in one system by the second, since IDs increment and are unique locally. Reading build-system name as the identifying name of that system, the policy retains both components and is the only offered policy distinguishing both collision cases. It is a naming policy, not a literal unsafe concatenation algorithm, arbitrary shared display-name guarantee, or native ACR-generated global identifier. The claimed single-system countercontext follows the same reasoning and documented build-ID meaning.

A locally unique build ID locates a run only with its producing CI/CD namespace known, as the unit ties IDs to the producing system. The stem allows overlapping sequences across two systems and gives no global allocation. Thus the bare ID cannot guarantee the required unique execution reference. It can suffice for the documented build-ID pattern within one known system whose run IDs are unique; that is deliberately not this context.

Tagging lines 25–29 explicitly supports stable release-line reuse for maintained base inputs. Reusing one such tag after each build violates the requested never-reused deployment reference even if its current value is accurate. That alternate maintenance use is sourced, but it cannot retain a distinct name for each producing deployment build.

A broader default affects unrelated work as well. The source distinguishes connection-wide settings from SET LOCAL within a transaction, which is the narrower requirement here.

The IVFFlat product example uses SET LOCAL inside BEGIN/COMMIT, and the pooling unit recommends transaction-local settings. This binds the tuning to the same transaction and avoids assumptions about later backend assignment.

sourceReviews.supportingSummary: A transaction pool returns backend connections between transactions, so subsequent work must not assume session affinity. SET LOCAL belongs inside the search transaction. Psycopg's pool.connection returns a checkout even on exceptional exit, and resilience uses bounded backoff. The unit's broader claims about automatic session resets and prepared statements are not used as universal contracts.

The product receipt separates exact non-ANN search from index approximation, requires dimensions on indexed vector columns, and pairs cosine <=> with vector_cosine_ops and L2 <-> with vector_l2_ops. HNSW has no IVFFlat training requirement. Crucially, probes equal to all lists is exact and the planner then does not use IVFFlat; one probe is not universally partial if there is one list. EXPLAIN ANALYZE measures execution and SET LOCAL scopes probes to a transaction.

choiceReviews.rationale: A setting made during startup belongs to whichever backend was obtained then. Transaction pooling does not promise that later transactions reuse that backend session.
A server-wide change extends beyond this one search transaction and can affect other workloads, violating the requested local scope.
BEGIN, SET LOCAL ivfflat.probes=12, the search and COMMIT keep the setting on the transaction's backend and let PostgreSQL discard that local override when the transaction finishes.

cloud_RoleName identifies the emitting service and the query retains the request and dependency values separately. Equating the origins fits same-service dependencies, not a row whose dependencyRole differs.

choiceReviews.rationale: operation_Id is the trace ID, shared across the whole span tree. Joining it establishes common trace membership; the separately projected role fields preserve each row's emitting service.
Parent span ID is distinct from trace ID. A same-trace dependency can be a grandchild or belong to another downstream branch, both permitted by this stem.
cloud_RoleName denotes the emitter of its own telemetry row. Renaming both sides retains their distinct origins; a join on trace ID does not rewrite dependencyRole to requestRole.

itemCount represents sampling weight. Summing yields estimated represented counts of 30 for TimeoutError and 8 for ValueError, matching the requested weighted-volume ranking.
avg describes the average sampling weight of a retained record. It can characterize weight differences but does not include how many records contribute to each exception type's represented total.

choiceReviews.rationale: max takes the largest individual weight: 10 and 1. It does not accumulate three or eight represented records into each type's volume.
